identificationModule.briefTitle: A Single-arm, Open-label, Single-center Prospective Study of Fruquintinib Combined With Envafolimab in the Treatment of Advanced or Unresectable Locally Advanced Bone and Soft Tissue Sarcoma

statusModule.whyStopped: Recruitment is temporarily suspended to allow for operational adjustments at the study sites. The trial will resume once all site readiness requirements are met

descriptionModule.briefSummary: Many osteosarcomas are cured with a variety of combined chemotherapy and surgery, but a significant number will still relapse.VEGF promotes an immunosuppressive microenvironment and contributes to immune checkpoint inhibitor resistance in cancer.We aimed to explore the efficacy and safety of fruquintinib combined immunotherapy for bone and soft tissue sarcoma.
descriptionModule.detailedDescription: A single-arm, open-label, single-center prospective study of fruquintinib combined with envafolimab in the treatment of advanced or unresectable locally advanced bone and soft tissue sarcoma.

conditions: Advanced or Unresectable Locally Advanced Bone and Soft Tissue Sarcoma
keywords: advanced or unresectable locally advanced bone and soft tissue sarcoma

interventions.name: fruquintinib
interventions.description: VEGF receptor tyrosine-kinase inhibitor：Fruquintinib 4 mg orally once daily on Days 1-14 of each 21-day cycle; dose may be adjusted by the investigator within 3-7 mg. Treatment continues until disease progression, death, or intolerable toxicity.

interventions.name: Envafolimab
interventions.description: anti-PD-1 immune checkpoint inhibitor：Envafolimab（400mg), subcutaneous injection, d1, Q3w，Until disease progression or intolerable toxicity occurs.

primaryOutcomes.description: The time from enrollment to disease progression or death.
